summary: Beginner tutorials for setting up, running and fine-tuning popular open-source LLMs on Linux, from Datawhale.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Self LLM (the 'Open-Source LLM User Guide') is a Datawhale tutorial collection for beginners, mainly in Chinese, on using open-source large models on Linux. It covers environment setup, deployment, command-line use, web demos, LangChain integration and fine-tuning for models such as LLaMA, ChatGLM and InternLM.
sixtySeconds.problem: Getting an open model running and fine-tuned involves many setup details. These tutorials walk through each step per model.
whoFor: Beginners learning to run open LLMs
Students in China learning model deployment
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for step-by-step, per-model guides from a well-known learning community, with example projects.
requirements: A Linux machine, ideally with a GPU

overview: Contents: environment configuration guides per model, deployment and usage tutorials for mainstream open LLMs, deployment and application guidance (command line, online demo, LangChain), and full and efficient fine-tuning (distributed full fine-tuning, LoRA, p-tuning).
The suggested order is environment setup first, then deployment and usage, then fine-tuning. Example projects include fine-tuned chat characters and a maths tutor model.
The tutorials are mostly in Chinese, with an English README. Apache 2.0 licensed.
